p066.text: A slam dunk and the crowds cheer!
A game of sports can be so exciting.
All over the world, people love watching sports, talking about sports and playing sports.
Can you guess why?
Ball sports are very popular.
For example, football.
Half of the world loves football.
That's almost four billion people.
Volleyball is another popular ball sport.
You probably know it.
But here in Laos they don't play volleyball with their hands and arms.
They play it with their feet, head and knees.
This game is called Sepak takraw – kick volleyball.
People love playing it in southeast Asia.
Dodgeball is another great ball game.
Do you play it at school?
You have to be very good at throwing and catching the ball.
Bowling uses a different kind of ball – a very hard ball.
You can't kick it.
You roll it and try to knock over the pins at the end of the lane.
Young and old people can play this game.
Do you know squash?
Lots of people like playing it.
Usually, it's a game between two players but you can also play in a team.
Players hit the ball against four walls, and it's a very quick sport!
But you have to be careful so you don't get hit.
What's your favourite sport?

p067.text: Nikolai Kutsenko, from Ukraine, can do amazing things with a football.
He can kick a ball well ... but he can also keep the ball in the air with his feet, legs and head.
Lots of footballers can do this.
But can they do it for 24 hours and 30 minutes without stopping?
Nikolai can and it's a world record!
Sloan Henderson, from Utah, is a really good snowboarder – and she's only 14 months old!
Her mother and father take her to the mountains, and they put her on a snowboard – and there she goes!
Sloan loves to be on the board.
People are often surprised when they see her because she doesn't fall over!
American rock-climber Maureen 'Mo' Beck was born without her left hand and only part of her left arm, but she can climb really well.
She is the winner of two climbing World Championships for disabled athletes, and five national championships.
She has her own special way of climbing, but Maureen thinks she is just the same as any other climber.
Goatee can't talk or write, but she can surf!
She surfs with her owner, Dana McGregor.
Dana helps Goatee to stand on the board and together they ride the waves in California.
Goatee wears a yellow life-jacket because she can't swim very well!
And now there is a children's book about her, too – Dana is the author.

p069.text: Hi, Julia. It's me, Mike.
Hi, Mike. How's it going?
Do you want to go cycling later today?
Go cycling? Good idea. What time?
How about after lunch? Say, two o'clock?
Two o'clock? No, sorry, I can't. I've got a taekwondo lesson at two.
OK, how about three o'clock?
No, the lesson only finishes at half past three.
OK, so how about four o'clock?
I can't. Mum wants to give me a tennis lesson at four.
Until what time?
I'm not sure. Maybe about quarter to five?
Really? But we can't go cycling then. It gets dark at half past four.
Well, yes, you're right. Sorry.
So maybe we can go cycling before lunch?
Um, I've got a school rugby match until about half past eleven.
What time does it start?
Ten o'clock.
Julia, it's quarter to ten now.
Really? I need to go. Let's go cycling tomorrow.
OK. Call me in the morning. See you. Have a good match.

p070.text: It's 15th February at Greece Athena High School, New York.
Jason McElwain is an 18-year-old student.
Jason is autistic.
He loves basketball and he helps with the school basketball team.
Jason practises hard every day, but he never plays in the team.
Tonight is the last game of the season.
It's Jason's last chance to play a game with the team, but for 44 minutes, he sits on the bench and watches.
It's four minutes before the end.
The team is winning, so the coach tells Jason to go out and play.
The team and the crowd are very happy, because everyone knows Jason and likes him.
Jason tries to score a basket, but he misses.
But suddenly he hits a 3-point basket.
The crowd goes crazy.
Jason hits another 3-pointer, then another and another – he hits six 3-pointers (it's a record for the team) and scores twenty points altogether.
The team wins, and Jason is a real hero.
It's an amazing night for him!
Soon Jason starts to become famous.
People in his town know who he is.
The US president comes to Jason's town to meet him.
Jason writes a book and some people want to make a film about him.
He becomes assistant coach to the high school basketball team.
Now Jason works hard to help other autistic people.
He travels across the US to help get money for autism research.

p072.text: Right! Have we got everything? Tennis rackets, balls …?
Yes, I think so. And we've got some food – sandwiches, fruit and stuff – and some water. So, let's go.
Just a minute! Oh, no! It's raining!
You're right. We can't play outside in the rain.
Why don't we go to the sports centre in town? They've got an indoor court.
No, it's always very busy. I'm sure we can't play there today.
Maybe you're right. It's a bit expensive, too.
OK, so we can't play today. It's no big deal. We can play tomorrow, perhaps.
Yes. But I'm a bit sad now.
Me, too. But what can we do? It's raining, and that's that.
I know! How about watching some old tennis games on the internet?
Good idea. I like watching really good players.
And we can eat our food.
Let's go and switch the computer on.

p073.text: Oh, hello. It's you. Sorry, I'm not feeling great.
Why? This is why. And I have a geography test tomorrow.
I like geography, but there's just so much information to learn.
How can I stay positive today?
But that's not the only problem.
Because I have a geography test tomorrow, I can't do all the things I really want to do today.
I can't play tennis with Tyler.
I can't go to see a movie with Tyler.
I can't watch baseball with Tyler.
I can't go for an ice cream with Tyler.
Tyler has a geography test tomorrow too, and Tyler's great at geography.
He's coming over to help me, and he's bringing popcorn.
That's what I always say, because if you stay positive, you can find an answer to any problem.

p110.text: Our lives move very fast today, especially in big cities.
But many years ago, that was different.
People couldn't jump on a bus or take the tube to work.
They walked.
For a long time, the fastest way of travelling was by horse or boat.
That changed with the steam engine in the 18th century.
Then came cars, motorcycles and, of course, airplanes.
So what's new and popular today?
E-scooters!
Electric scooter sharing is the new way to get around.
They are taking over the world's big cities.
They are fun and easy to use.
You don't have to buy one.
You rent one.
All you need is to log on to an app and then, off you go.
They are cheaper than taxis.
You can get around traffic jams.
And you don't have to do any hard work, like on a bike.
They aren't bad for the environment either.
But is that true?
Well, these e-scooters don't last very long.
In Paris, some e-scooters break after one month.
Many people are unhappy because there are too many e-scooters.
They block the pavements and drive into people.
Because people are angry about e-scooters, they throw them into rivers or break them.
Is that the answer?
What do you think of e-scooters?
Do you like them?

p111.text: A lot of big cities, like London, have got many traffic problems.
Sometimes a journey of a few kilometres can take more than an hour.
So what's the best way to get across London?
For a very short journey, it's probably a good idea to walk.
But what happens when you want to go further?
The presenters of a popular TV show about cars decided to find out.
Each of the presenters chose a different type of transport to make the same 27-kilometre journey.
One presenter went by bike.
One went by car.
Another chose public transport – the underground and bus – and the last one travelled by speedboat up the River Thames.
They all started at the same time and the same place in West London, but who got to City Airport in East London first?
The results were a surprise.
The bike came first.
In second place was the speedboat.
Public transport came third and the car was last.
So the presenters had an answer.
The bike was quicker than all the other types of transport and the car was slower.
They weren't very happy with the result because they wanted the car to win.
They made a joke and said the bike wasn't a real winner because it was more dangerous.
But, of course, the bike is the real winner.
It's the best way to get about.
It's cheaper than public transport and it is healthier than going by car.
It's also better for our cities because bikes don't make the air dirty.
So next time you need to travel around, think before you and your parents get into the car – 'Can we make this journey by bike?'

p113.text: I want to go to Windsor.
It only stops at Clapham Junction and Windsor.
There's one at half past ten, but that's a slower train.
I'm not in a hurry, and I don't want to run.
What time does that one arrive in Windsor?
And how often are the trains to Windsor?
And how much is a ticket?
Do you want a single or a return?
Then you can get an off-peak day return ticket for £12.70.
It's cheaper than the anytime day return.
I'd like the off-peak day return one then.
What platform does the train leave from?
And what platform does it arrive at in Windsor?
My friend wants to meet me there.
But Windsor is a very small station, a lot smaller than Waterloo.
There are only two platforms at Windsor.
OK, then that's not a problem.

p114.text: My favourite journey. We all love going on a journey.
Here are some of your favourites. Thank you for sharing them!
Adam. I love boats and my favourite boat journey is the one by ferry across the Danube River.
My grandma lives in Budapest.
When I visit her, we often go on it together.
It's not a long journey.
It's only ten minutes.
The ferry just takes you across the river to the other side of the city.
We don't get off the boat.
We just go there and back again.
Rose!
I really love steam trains.
There's one in Scotland.
It goes from Fort William to Mallaig on the west coast, and it's called the Jacobite Steam Train.
It's the famous one you see in the Harry Potter films.
The one that takes Harry and his classmates to Hogwarts. But that's not why I like it.
I like the sound it makes and I like the view from the window.
It travels past lakes and mountains and beautiful beaches.
What's my favourite journey?
My journey to school.
We live in a village and my school is in the next village.
Every morning, I walk across the fields and then along the river until I'm at school.
It's a really beautiful walk.
I love looking for birds.
There are some lovely ones.
And sometimes, if I'm lucky, I see a rabbit.
I love my walk to school.
But I love the walk home more!
Max. My favourite journey is a very fast bike ride.
My grandparents have a house in the mountains. There is a road down the mountain to the town.
It goes down very fast, and it goes through a big forest.
Every morning, we ride down to the town to get bread.
It only takes ten minutes to ride down, but it takes a lot longer to ride back up again!

p117.text: Transport around the world.
The Amfibus, the Netherlands.
The big, blue Amfibus certainly makes a big splash!
It's in Rotterdam, and it takes people on tours of the city.
It's cool.
It can travel on land and in the water.
It is more expensive than water taxis, but it is more exciting, too.
It is slower in the water than on land.
It goes at 8 kilometres per hour in the water and 96 kilometres per hour on land.
The tour lasts for an hour, and it costs 27.50 euros.
Moving walkways and escalators, Hong Kong.
The Central-Mid-Levels Escalator is 800 metres long.
Escalators are usually inside a shopping centre or an airport, but not this one!
It's outside.
It's a great way to travel round this city of hills.
And it's free!
There are 14 places where you can get on and off.
The escalators travel down the hill from 6am to 10am, so people can travel to work.
They travel up the hill from 10am to midnight.
The urban cable car, Turkey.
Ankara's cable car is cheaper than other forms of public transport.
It is healthier because it doesn't pollute the air.
It is also easier and quicker than travelling by car, because there are no traffic jams in the sky!
It travels 60 metres above the ground, and passengers can get great views of the city.
Submarines, Lanzarote and Tenerife.
Now you can travel in a submarine!
This submarine carries tourists.
It is a safe and comfortable way to see the colourful fish and the plants and rocks under our seas.
The submarine can carry 48 people, and it has 11 large windows on each side.
It travels down 60 metres under the sea.

p202.text: People use different types of transport to get from one place to the next.
In Wuppertal, a city in Germany, the 'Schwebebahn' or suspension railway is very special.
The first track opened in 1901.
It is the oldest electric elevated railway with hanging cars in the world.
More than 85,000 passengers use it every day.
There are lots of special cars in Cuba, especially in Havana.
Most of them are very old.
But these yellow taxis are much newer.
They are called cocotaxis because they look like coconuts.
They are a great way of getting around.
Tourists love them!
Tourists also like riding down the hills in Madeira, Portugal, on the Monte Toboggan.
Originally, people used these sledges to transport food and other things.
Today, they transport people.
Two 'carreiros', or sledge drivers, run next to the sledge and keep it on the street.
They wear special shoes.
When the ride gets too fast, the drivers can use their shoes to slow it down.
This strange form of transportation is called zorbing or globe-riding.
And yes, a person is inside!
The first zorbing site was in New Zealand.
But now you can go zorbing all over the world.
Even on water.
What's a popular way of getting around in your city?
